messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] smooth and time
parts:
Dear Julia,
If only the mean is non-stationary, and that non-stationarity is just a trend, the linear term you included may be enough. Forecasting this kind of data usually needs more than just linear.trend + zero.mean.random.random effect. Have you tried to build in some seasonality?
Best regards,
Elias



On Fri, 22 Oct 2021 at 10:51, 'Julia Kondrasch' via R-inla discussion group <r-inla-disc...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Hi,

I am new to Inla and has some questions. I am trying to modeling CPI (german consumer price Index - from 1995 to 2021, monthly) with bayesian penalized Splines (with RW1 and RW2) with differenent priors. And then forecast 12 month. This Data ist stationary.  
 I checked out, that I can't do forecast with rw1/rw2 Splines, Is this Right?
 e.g. 
y<- CPI$B (monthly consumer price index)
time<-  (from 1995 to 2021, monthly)
CPI.Group<-inla.group(CPI$B, n=20, method="quantile")

result<-inla(y~-1+time+f(CPI.Group, model="rw2", data=CPI,  constr = FALSE, hyper=prec.prior),
              data = CPI, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), family = "gaussian",
              control.compute=list(   dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, waic=TRUE))

Is this Example possible:

result1 <- inla(y ~ -1 + f(CPI.Group, model = "rw1",scale.model = T, constr = FALSE, hyper=prec.prior4)+f(time, model = "ar1"),
                data = CPI, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), 
              family = "gaussian",
              control.family = list(hyper=list(prec=list(param=c(1,0.2))))) 


Can I use Inla? Should I use Space-Time Model, with stationary? Can you give me please some advise? 

Thank you very much.
Kind regards,
Julia
